articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

Growth in the core industrial sectors of the economy climbed to a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, driven by a surge in electricity generation, and coal, cement, and iron ore production, and a low base effect, official data released on Friday (November 20, 2026) showed.

Data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on the Index of Core Industries shows that growth in October surpassed the 8.2% in September, the previous series high. The new index, released this year with a base year of 2022-23, has data that goes back only up to April 2024.
However, the data also shows that the strong growth figure in October was also likely aided by the fact that the index grew a relatively poor 0.8% in October last year.

“While core output surged by 10.9% in October 2026, the fastest pace in the new series, this was supported by a low base related to the shift in the festive calendar, with output having expanded by a marginal 0.8% in the year ago month,” Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA said.

“While the growth print for October 2026 signals a strong start for the third quarter of FY2027, this is largely optical,” Ms. Nayar added. “The average performance for October-November 2026 would provide a better assessment, as this would adjust for festive base effects.”

Within the index, the coal sector saw growth accelerating to 23.05% in October 2026, far faster than the 10.7% registered in September. October’s performance, however, is likely also due to low base effect, since the sector contracted 8.4% in October last year.

articles.title: Following Cyclone Akvan, monsoon rain to resume over T.N. from tomorrow
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall in coastal districts, including Chennai and Cuddalore, and mild rainfall over adjoining areas; wet weather likely to last till the first week of December

Following Cyclone Akvan’s passage on Friday morning, most parts of Tamil Nadu are likely to experience a brief break in monsoon activity, accompanied by a dip in night-time temperatures. Wet weather is expected to return on Sunday and intensify over the subsequent days.
The break in rainfall is expected to raise day temperatures by two or three degrees Celsius in a few pockets of the State.
The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has also forecast ground frost at isolated places in the Nilgiris and Kodaikanal till Sunday.

The absence of widespread rainfall has pushed various districts, including Tiruvarur, Thanjavur, Madurai, Salem, and Chengalpattu, into the rainfall deficit category. The State has so far received nearly 26 cm of monsoon rainfall, which is 14% lower than its seasonal share since October 1.
RMC officials said Cyclone Akvan was expected to weaken into a depression on Friday, and gradually fade away.

V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said dry and cold northwesterly winds and the absence of cloud cover and rainfall led to a rise in day temperatures and drop in minimum temperatures over most parts of the State.

A trough in the easterly wave is likely to revive rainfall activity from Sunday and bring intense rainfall from Monday as it moves across the State. While coastal districts are expected to benefit more, interior Tamil Nadu is also likely to receive moderate rainfall till November 26.
“We are expecting wet weather in the State till December first week, with a low pressure area likely to form then. The sustained rainfall activity may narrow rainfall deficit,” he said.
The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall over coastal districts, including Chennai, Cuddalore, and Nagapattinam, on Sunday and mild rainfall over areas adjoining coastal districts.
On Monday, rainfall is expected to intensify over 10 coastal districts, including Cuddalore, Thoothukudi, and Kanniyakumari.
While the wet spell would cover the entire State, intensity of rainfall would vary. For instance, districts such as Chennai, Ranipet, Villupuram, and Karur would receive moderate rainfall.

For November 24, the RMC has issued yellow alert to coastal districts from Tiruvallur to Kanniyakumari, indicating heavy rainfall, with wind speeds of up to 50 kmph. Interior and Western Ghats districts are expected to receive moderate rainfall.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

A mathematician at AI company Anthropic said Friday (November 20, 2026) that he had used the firm’s Claude chatbot to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a problem that has eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years.
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpoge wrote in a four-page note released Friday (November 20, 2026).
The claim has not been independently verified, and the proof has not yet been reviewed by outside experts.

First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
It is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000, which offers $1 million for a solution to each.
Under the institute’s rules, a solution must be published in a peer-reviewed journal and withstand two years of scrutiny.
Mr. Alpoge said the method also resolves a broader version of the problem known as the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis.

He said he and Claude had produced a version of the proof in Lean, a programming language that allows mathematical arguments to be checked by a computer, and that he was releasing only that version for now.
A full written argument would be extremely long, he said, adding that he had not yet mastered all of the mathematics involved and planned to write it up properly.

Mr. Alpoge said he had consulted Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei before announcing the result and acknowledged that its timing could be viewed cynically, without elaborating, though he was probably referring to this week’s record IPO.
In August, Anthropic said an unreleased version of Claude had improved a long-standing result related to the Riemann Hypothesis, while stressing that it had not proved it.
Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment from AFP.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

articles.title: Outlook outage: On Microsoft and dangers of centralising digital systems
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

articles.title: Advocates, traders protest in Vaniyambadi for additional district court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town
Advocates, traders and residents staged a protest near a bus terminus in Vaniyambadi town on Thursday, demanding an additional district court and a permanent building for the court complex.

The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon, when it could be risky to conduct court proceedings at the dilapidated Judicial Magistrate court. “Work to build a permanent court complex should be expedited. An additional district court should also be set up in the court complex”, said A.C. Devakumar, president, Bar Association (Vaniyambadi).

At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town. Each court, on an average, is located at least 1.5 km away from the other court. It has resulted in hardship for litigants, advocates, and court staff to commute from one court to another as some petitioners have cases in different courts that will be taken up on the same day.

The Judicial Magistrate Court, the oldest among three courts, was located in the Government Estate since the 1920s. The District Munsif court, formed in 1995, was functioning from a rented room in the Government Commercial Tax building. The subordinate court that was created in 2009 was also operating from a rented room in the town.

Every day, on an average, more than 150 litigants, mostly from Vaniyambadi taluk that comprises 45 villages, visit these courts. Around 75 advocates are working as regular practitioners. On an average, over 100 cases come up at each court every day. Currently, 1,500 - 2,000 cases are pending before each of these three courts.

Case bundles and court records get damaged during monsoon as the building is inundated. The court also does not have an audio system, to call for cases or parties. As a result, many litigants wait for long hours or leave as they are unsure about whether their case has been called.

articles.title: Kerala High Court disposes of PILs against reconstitution of Waqf Board
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court had refused to stay the reconstitution of the board in October
A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday disposed of all public interest litigations (PILs) related to the reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board.

The Bench observed that the reconstitution of the board had given rise to a fresh cause of action, following which the aggrieved parties had filed writ petitions. It said the petitions were required to be heard by a Single Judge in accordance with the roster.

The High Court had in October refused to stay the reconstitution of the board. The court was considering appeals filed by former board chairperson K.S. Hamza and member C.K. Usman Haji against a Single Bench order refusing to stay the reconstitution.
The court had then held that a stay could not be granted as the new board had taken charge. The State had reconstituted the board on October 16 and nominated nine new members.

fullParagraphs: A 19-year-old B.Tech student of Vellore Institute of Technology Chennai, was found dead in the bathroom of the boy’s hostel, early on Thursday. The police are investigating whether it is a case of suicide.

articles.title: Set aside differences and oppose Mekedatu dam, says TNCC president
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He also questions Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s silence when Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke in favour of the project in his presence

Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore on Thursday said the party would oppose the proposed Mekedatu dam across the Cauvery and called for all political parties in Tamil Nadu to unite against the project instead of indulging in mutual accusations.
He said the project could spell a death knell for the Cauvery delta and turn the region drought-prone. The Congress was clear that it would not compromise on Tamil Nadu’s legitimate rights, he said.

Calling for a united stand, he urged Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin, Edappadi K. Palaniswami, and O. Panneerselvam to join hands in opposing the project. He also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s silence when Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar spoke in favour of the project in his presence.

Referring to the recent meeting between three Tamil Nadu Ministers and Union Minister C.R. Paatil, Mr. Tagore said the State government should share the outcome of the discussions with the Assembly, its alliance partners, and the people.

Mr. Tagore also criticised the AIADMK for not participating in the all-party meeting and meeting of MPs convened by the Tamil Nadu government on delimitation, while subsequently supporting the Assembly resolution on the issue.

On the Congress-TVK relationship, he said the prominence given to Mr. Vijay at Sonia Gandhi’s book launch in Delhi reflected the strong and long-term ties between the two parties. He added that the Congress was committed to helping the government fulfil its promise of building a strong and drug-free Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Speakers recall Sathya Sai Baba’s emphasis on vital role of women in society
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Noted actor Rashmika Mandanna and former Chief Secretary to Government of Karnataka Vandita Sharma participate in the Ladies’ Day observed as part of the ongoing birth centenary celebrations of Sri Sathya Sai Baba in Puttaparthi
Noted actor Rashmika Mandanna participated in the Ladies’ Day observed as part of the ongoing birth centenary celebrations of Sri Sathya Sai Baba, at Prashanti Nilayam in Puttaparthi on Thursday.

Apart from the cultural presentations, speakers who addressed the gathering in Sai Kulwant Hall highlighted Sri Sathya Sai Baba’s emphasis on the dignity, inner strength and vital role of women in society.

The girl students of the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Learning, Anantapur campus, presented a band performance. Vandita Sharma, former Chief Secretary to the Government of Karnataka, and Neelam Desai, senior cardiac surgeon at the Sri Sathya Sai Institute of Higher Medical Sciences, Prasanthigram, participated in the traditional lighting of the lamp marking the occasion.

Delivering the welcome address, Dr. Neelam Desai recalled Sri Sathya Sai Baba’s message on the first Ladies’ Day, observed on November 19, 1995. “Among human beings, it is a privilege to be born as a woman,” she said quoting Sri Sathya Sai Baba, and highlighted the qualities of love, sacrifice, courage and perseverance that women embody.

She shared the story of Ramabai Ranveer, a 47-year-old mother from Ambajogai, Maharashtra, who won a local barefoot running event to earn ₹3,000 for books and educational supplies for her daughters. She also recalled Samudra Pradakshina, the pioneering all-women tri-service circumnavigation sailing expedition flagged off on September 11, 2025.
Girl students of Sri Sathya Sai Higher Secondary School and Smt. Eswaramma High School presented cultural offerings as part of the morning programme.

Addressing the gathering, Ms. Vandita Sharma noted that Ladies’ Day celebrates women’s inherent strength and contributions to family and society, while encouraging them to recognise their potential and express it with confidence and commitment.

She appreciated the Sri Sathya Sai Media Centre for making Baba’s discourses readily accessible, enabling devotees to draw guidance from His teachings. She urged everyone to put His message into practice in daily life.

Ms. Rashmika Mandanna shared how her association with the family of actor Vijay Deverakonda had brought her closer to Baba and His teachings. Spending time with the family, she said, had helped her understand their devotion and appreciate the relevance of Baba’s message.
She emphasised the importance of spiritual and emotional strength, along with an unwavering commitment to human values.

articles.title: Anthropic soars in Wall Street debut despite AI jitters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in the offering. The IPO price valued the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares. At around $98 a share, the company was worth about $1.8 trillion

Anthropic shares opened 34% higher in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday (November 19, 2026), briefly valuing the AI giant around $2 trillion, as investors shrugged off the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble.

The shares opened at $111.50 before settling minutes into trading at around $98, up 18% from the $83 at which the company priced its shares on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), already above its expected range.

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in the offering. The IPO price valued the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares. At around $98 a share, the company was worth about $1.8 trillion.

The debut marks a milestone in the AI boom. A company founded five years ago by OpenAI defectors worried about AI safety has become the first of the leading model developers to list on Wall Street, at a valuation rivalling decades-old tech brands.
The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” gives ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

“Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” chief executive Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq in New York’s Times Square, underlining the company’s priority of promoting safe AI.
The offering surpasses the $75 billion that Elon Musk’s SpaceX raised in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.

SpaceX’s total ultimately rose to $86 billion after its underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares. Anthropic has granted its underwriters a similar option, which would lift its total to about $93.5 billion.

“This may be the breath of fresh air that the tech trade needed to move beyond the fog of artificial intelligence that we’ve been living in for the last couple of weeks,” Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management told AFP .
The strong demand comes even as AI stocks have swung sharply, with investors questioning whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

Nvidia, the chip giant at the centre of the AI investment boom and an investor in Anthropic and dozens of other AI companies, has been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after a reported affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
Anthropic’s Claude models are among the most powerful in the world, hailed for their problem-solving potential but also feared for their capacity to destabilise societies and replace human workers.

fullParagraphs: The Claude maker priced its shares at $83 apiece, implying an equity valuation of about $1.03 trillion based on outstanding shares, with trading scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19

Anthropic, the maker of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot Claude, has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 a share, valuing the offering at approximately $81.34 billion, according to an announcement by the company on November 18.

The company said its shares were expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary closing conditions.

According to Anthropic’s announcement, the offering comprises 980 million shares of Class A common stock. Of these, 956.35 million shares are being sold by the company and 23.65 million by existing shareholders. Anthropic said it would not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the selling shareholders.

At the IPO price of $83 a share, the company’s portion of the offering is valued at approximately $79.38 billion, while the shares sold by existing shareholders are valued at approximately $1.96 billion. These figures are before underwriting discounts and expenses.
At $83 a share, Anthropic’s overall equity value works out to approximately $1.03 trillion, based on the total number of shares outstanding after the IPO.
Anthropic has also given the banks (underwriters) managing the IPO the option to purchase an additional 147 million shares within 30 days, potentially increasing the size of the offering.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters for the IPO, with JPMorgan, Citigroup, Barclays and other investment banks also participating, according to the SEC filing.
The IPO comes amid growing investor concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and whether technology companies can generate sufficient returns from their infrastructure spending.
On November 5, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%, wiping out trillions of dollars in market value, while NVIDIA shares declined 9% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12%.

Earlier, on October 29, Alphabet shares plunged 12.6%, wiping out approximately $500 billion in market value after its quarterly results raised concerns over its advertising business and the cash-flow impact of rising AI investments. The sell-off reflected broader concerns over the valuations of AI-linked companies and the returns from their heavy spending on data centres and computing infrastructure.
The broader U.S. market opened higher on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite gaining 1.55% at the opening bell at 9.30 am U.S. Eastern Time (8 pm IST), according to Reuters.

Anthropic’s shares had yet to begin trading as of 10.45 am US ET (9.15 pm IST), with The Wall Street Journal reporting that early indications pointed to an opening price of around $104, about 25% above the IPO price of $83. Reuters had earlier reported an indicative price of $99.82 at 9.50 a.m. U.S. ET (8.20 p.m. IST).

articles.title: FIR against two former Bengal Ministers over sexual assault charges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Five former Ministers, who had been part of Mamata Banerjee’s cabinet, have been arrested since the BJP government came to power in May 2026

articles.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ updates: Three lakh evacuated, 423 rescue teams deployed as cyclone heads to Odisha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The severe cyclonic storm is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by noon on November 20

The Disaster Management Unit of Union Ministry of Communications has instructed telecom service providers to activate Intra Circle Roaming facility in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur and Khordha district on November 20.

As per information provided by Odisha Space Applications Centre, as many as 941 places have been identified as landslip prone areas including 211 in Gajapati district, Ganjam (169), Rayagada (169), Kandhamal (163) Koraput (151) and Malkangiri (78), said Mr. Pujari while reviewing preparation for cyclone “Akvan” on November 19, 2026.

Ghat roads (hill passes) such as Kalinga and Gajalbadi connecting Ganjam and Kandhamal districts have been barricaded, apprehending landslides. Red warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall has been issued for districts such as Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Puri, Ganjam, Gajapati, and Kandhamal.

“Water Resources Department has started depleting reservoirs in districts to be affected by the cyclone. Engineers are continuously monitoring situation while technical teams have been deployed. Two gates of major dam and 23 gates of different medium irrigation dams are kept opened,” said Odisha Chief Secretary Anu Garg. - Satyasundar Barik

Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved northwards at a speed of 13 kmph during the past six hours and was centred over the same region at 5.30 p.m. on November 19, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The cyclone is likely to move north-northwestwards and cross North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by noon on November 20.

Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari informed that senior bureaucrats were assigned different districts to monitor rescue-and-restoration activities, besides monitoring situations from State Emergency Operation Centres. In Ganjam and Gajapati districts, 17 satellite phones were provided to key persons to remain in contact if communication network is snapped due to cyclone.

As part of the preparedness measures, 70 Cell-on-Wheels (CoW) units, 197 Mobile Diesel Generator (DG) sets and 61 support teams have been deployed to strengthen telecom infrastructure and ensure continuity of communication during the cyclone. The Disaster Management Unit of Union Ministry of Communications has instructed telecom service providers to activate Intra Circle Roaming facility in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur and Khordha district on November 20. - Satyasundar Barik

Odisha on Thursday (November 19, 2026) geared up to tackle Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, which is expected to cross the State’s coast near Gopalpur by noon on November 20, with heavy rain and maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph. The State shifted close to three lakh people to safer places by evening.

As many as 60 units Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force, 14 units of National Disaster Response Force and 221 teams of State fire services have been positioned at vulnerable areas to carry out rescue and restoration operation soon after ‘Akvan’ passed through the State.

“The severe cyclonic storm “Akvan” over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved northwards with the speed of 13 kmph during past six hours and lay centered over the same region about 270 km south-southeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 350 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha), 380 km east of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 420 km south of Puri (Odisha) and 640 km east-northeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu),” said India Meteorological Department in its 8 p.m. bulletin on Thursday.

“It is likely to move north-northwestward and cross North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur, by noon of November 20, 2026 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph,” it said.

articles.title: Trinamool party symbol row: Abhishek Banerjee says twin flower symbol will return in seven days
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee said that the symbol does not belong to either faction and Mr. Banerjee will not be able to stake claim over the symbol in seven births

The two rival factions of the Trinamool Congress have become embroiled in a war of words over the party’s twin-flower symbol that has been frozen by the Election Commission of India (ECI). Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress on November 18 said that the original electoral symbol of the party will ultimately remain with Mamata Banerjee.

“The original name and electoral symbol had always been with Mamata Banerjee and will continue to remain so in the future. Just wait for seven days. We will prove how manipulations were made in filing affidavits to establish the right over the original party name and original electoral symbol. We will display that on the big screen,” Mr. Banerjee told media persons.

Mr. Banerjee has claimed that the faction of the party led by Ritabrata Banerjee filed affidavits with the help of the West Bengal Police. The Diamond Harbour MP had claimed that the alleged attack on his residence on November 7 was intended to interfere with the filing of affidavits, staking a claim over the affidavits.

Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee said that the symbol does not belong to either faction and Mr. Banerjee will not be able to stake claim over the symbol in seven births.
“He has said that they will get the symbol in seven days, they will not get the symbol in seven births,” the LOP, which represents the Democratic Trinamool Congress, said.

The ECI on September 17, 2026, had barred both factions, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the party, from using the party symbol and name in the bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar in West Bengal which were scheduled on October 6. The very next day, on September 18, the Mamata faction got the name ‘Mamata All India Trinamool Congress’ with ‘football player’ as its symbol , while the Ritabrata grouping was allotted the name ‘Democratic Trinamool Congress’ with the symbol ‘envelope’.

Both the factions of the Trinamool Congress have submitted truckloads of affidavits to the ECI, which includes support by party members, MPs and MLAs. Ritabrata Banerjee claims support of 65 of the 80 MLAs of the party. The faction of Mamata Banerjee has the support of a handful of MLAs and MPs who have not defected to NCPI or joined the BJP after the West Bengal Assembly polls of 2026.

articles.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The shares ended the session at around $97, up from an IPO price of $83, after opening at $111.50 and briefly valuing the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $2 trillion

Anthropic shares closed about 17% higher on their first day of trading on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as investors shrugged off the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble to snap up the AI giant’s stock after a record-breaking IPO.
The shares ended the session at around $97, up from an IPO price of $83, after opening at $111.50 and briefly valuing the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $2 trillion.

The debut marks a milestone in the AI boom. A company founded five years ago by OpenAI defectors worried about AI safety has become the first of the leading model developers to list on Wall Street, at a valuation rivalling decades-old tech brands.
The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” gives ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

SpaceX’s total ultimately rose to $86 billion after its underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares. Anthropic has granted its underwriters a similar option, which would lift its total to about $93.5 billion.

“This may be the breath of fresh air that the tech trade needed to move beyond the fog of artificial intelligence that we’ve been living in for the last couple of weeks,” Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management told AFP .
The strong demand comes even as AI stocks have swung sharply, with investors questioning whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

Nvidia, the chip giant at the centre of the AI investment boom and an investor in Anthropic and dozens of other AI companies, has been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after a reported affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
Anthropic’s Claude models are among the most powerful in the world, hailed for their problem-solving potential but also feared for their capacity to destabilise societies and replace human workers.
The five-year-old company’s revenue has surged at a pace few U.S. companies have ever matched, reaching $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier.
Much of that revenue comes from customers paying to use its AI models for computer coding. Its massive computing costs remain a major question for investors.
Anthropic has disclosed about $900 billion in commitments for computing capacity and warned in its filing that it must make many of those payments even if demand falls short.

articles.title: Draft of COP31 cover text drops references to fossil fuel phase-out, net zero dates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated

The latest iteration of the COP 31 draft cover text has eliminated references to fossil fuel phase-out and net-zero dates but has also deleted references to a firm $120 billion adaptation-finance target that developing countries have been asking for as “legally binding financial obligations” on developed countries. This suggests that the most ambitious demands of both the developed and developing country blocs have been eliminated.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome it needs the consensus of all Parties. The Presidency has said earlier drafts were not meant to reflect consensus.

The COP31 Presidency’s revised draft cover decision, dated November 19, has 80 paragraphs, down from 144 in the November 16 version. The summit officially ends on November 20, though negotiations frequently overshoot into the weekend.

A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated.

However, a widely expected outcome of raising electricity’s share in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035, scaling up the use of carbon capture utilisation technologies and making early warning systems universal by 2027, continue to find mention in the text. A broad commitment to triple adaptation finance also remains.

“ The draft cover text weaves the 35% electricity in final energy consumption by 2035, alongside tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling the rate of energy efficiency improvement by 2030, ” Ajay Mathur, India’s lead negotiator at Paris COP and former DG, International Solar Alliance, said in a statement. The electricity use in India went up by 13% in 2025 due to the Hormuz crisis alone. It will be an ambitious goal for India to achieve 35% electrification by 2035, but due to the increasing amount of renewable energy in the Indian energy mix, we will be near the 32-34% mark by 2035. ”

“We’re down to the wire at COP31, and the latest texts are alarmingly far from ambitious or equitable,” said Rachel Cleetus, Climate Program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists (UCS) in a statement. “Rich nations, most notably the EU nations, are still holding a harsh line against committing to tripling adaptation finance to at least $120 billion annually by 2035. Instead of reaching agreement on urgently needed climate finance, some countries seem willing to push negotiations toward failure.”

articles.title: Nearing 3 years as Rajasthan CM, Bhajan Lal Sharma seeks to assert his authority
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Having entered office with virtually no administrative experience, his tenure has been a continuous tightrope walk between balancing the demands of the party’s central leadership and build authority of his own within the State.

When Bhajan Lal Sharma, a first-time MLA who had largely remained in the background of the BJP’s Rajasthan unit, was named Chief Minister in December 2023, Congress State president Govind Singh Dotasara dismissed him as the “Parchi CM”, a leader chosen by the party’s central leadership rather than one who had built a political base of his own.

Nearly three years later, Mr. Dotasara has changed his line of attack. He now accuses the Mr. Sharma of being a leader “jisne poori BJP ko Rajasthan me khatam kar dala” (who has finished off the entire BJP in Rajasthan).

National & Polity Report: Nearing 3 years as Rajasthan CM, Bhajan Lal Sharma seeks to assert his authority. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.

articles.title: Nashik Court grants bail to Imtiaz Jaleel in TCS case on ₹50,000 bond
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: When Mr. Jaleel sought bail, the state opposed, but the court granted release on bond since the sections allow bail

The Nashik District and Sessions Court on Thursday (November 19, 2026) granted bail to AIMIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel, a co-accused in the TCS conversion and harassment case, after he appeared before the court and submitted a bond of ₹50,000, following the prosecution’s opposition to his plea.

When Mr. Jaleel appeared before the court to file the application for bail, the counsel representing the state opposed the plea, but the court approved the release upon the submission of the bond because the sections invoked against him permit release on bail.
The investigation into the TCS case established that Nida Khan evaded law enforcement for two months by staying in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

During the probe into the shelter provided to Khan, officials questioned MIM corporator Matin Patel to determine who directed him. The retrieval of evidence from devices and items led the police to name Jaleel, Patel, and individuals associated with them as co-accused in the case for providing assistance to a person evading law enforcement.

articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet okays confiscation of book that ‘insults’ Basavanna and ‘distorts’ his philosophy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Basava Samiti has accused U.S.-based author Ravi Hanj of hurting the sentiments of followers of the 12th century social reformer Basavanna in his book ‘Basava Mantapa’

With several Veerashaiva-Lingayat community leaders up in arms against the book Basava Mantapa, alleging that it distorts the teachings and philosophy of Basavanna and insults him, the Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday decided to confiscate copies of the book by Ravi Hanj, which are in circulation. It has also cleared action against publisher-journalist Vishveshwar Bhat.

After a prolonged discussion in the Cabinet meeting, a decision to confiscate the book and take legal action against the author was arrived at, announced Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara. “Normally, we do not take swift action based on petitions. But in this case a decision was taken since its impact is likely to be felt across the State,” he said.

Earlier in the day, the Basava Samiti not only demanded a ban of the book, but also filed a police complaint seeking action against the author and the publisher. In a social media post, BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra had also sought action against the publisher and the author.

When asked why an expert committee was not set up and an immediate decision taken after the samiti petitioned Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the Deputy Chief Minister said that senior Ministers had discussed the issue in the Cabinet meeting. “This is only the inittial reaction and we will look into the legality later. Action has been taken as per the provisions of BNS. We could not be silent spectators,” he said.

Addressing a press conference in Bengaluru, Basava Samiti president Aravind Jatti said the book hurt the sentiments of the Lingayat community and Basavanna’s followers in the name of research. He also called for criminal cases to be registered against those responsible for disturbing peace in society.

“Mr. Hanj has attacked Basavanna, who propagated the ideals of equality, a casteless society, the dignity of labour and the concept of a parliament, by describing him in derogatory terms. However, following the backlash, he is now trying to apologise and promise corrections. We want neither. They have mistaken the peaceful nature of the Veerashaiva-Lingayat community for weakness. It is condemnable that the book has been presented as a work of research to disguise its objectionable content,” he said.
“What is happening now is an ideological conspiracy aimed at undermining the Sharana philosophy and Lingayat identity. We know who is behind it,” he said.
Mr. Jatti alleged that such objectionable developments had intensified since the government declared Basavanna the “cultural leader of Karnataka.”

Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil warned that attacks on Basavanna and the Lingayat community would no longer be tolerated. “We will take to the street and launch an intense agitation. Protests have already begun in several parts of Karnataka,” he said.

“It is condemnable that Veerashaiva Mahasabha president Shankar Bidari and former Kannada Sahitya Parishat president Manu Baligar attended the launch of such a book. It is up to the Veerashaiva Mahasabha to decide what action should be taken against Mr. Bidari,” he said.

MLA for Aland B.R. Patil said, “There have always been elements that cannot tolerate the ideals of Basavanna, Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar. Mr. Hanj has written the book with malicious intent and attempted to tarnish Basavanna’s reputation.”
Former Mayor of the London Borough of Lambeth, Neeraj Patil, and thinker J. S. Patil also called for stringent action against the author and the publisher.

articles.title: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Squally winds of 40–50 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, along and off the West Bengal coast will prevail till Friday noon and ease afterward, with very rough sea conditions, says IMD
Several districts in the southern part of West Bengal, including Kolkata, will receive heavy rainfall until November 21 due to the cyclonic storm Akvan.

articles.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Anthropic’s debut fails to revive AI fervour
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: All three major U.S. stock indexes ended the session ⁠sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses
U.S. stocks slumped on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after Anthropic’s super-sized IPO ‌failed to revitalise faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its ​share price ebbed.
All three major U.S. stock indexes ended the session ⁠sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses.
The S&P 500 was on course to post its steepest weekly loss since April 2025.

Anthropic’s debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced ‌on late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened at $111.50 shortly ‌before noon. After the company’s market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began ‌to lose ⁠steam.
“The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager ⁠at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri.
Even so, Ellerbroek’s enthusiasm for ‌the AI trade has waned.

“My beliefs about the growth in data centre capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two,” he added. “Nvidia’s crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact. Data centres are ‌going to be more expensive to build and they’re going to be built more ​slowly.”
Advanced Micro Devices shares tumbled after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.
Most chipmakers were ⁠lower, including Micron and Broadcom, among others.
Nvidia marked its sixth straight session of losses after the chipmaker’s upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed lower. Neocloud firms CoreWeave ‌and Nebius sustained steep losses.
In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks shares jumped after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance. Walmart dipped after the retail giant’s annual sales forecast disappointed investors.

articles.title: The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home?

The Rohingya question has returned to the centre of international attention following the landmark judgment delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on November 19, 2026. Yet, for more than a million Rohingya living outside Myanmar, legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home? The crisis also exposes the international community’s inability to translate diplomatic declarations, humanitarian assistance and legal proceedings into a sustainable political settlement.

When I began working on Myanmar in the United Nations Department of Political Affairs in 2011, the Rohingya question was largely confined to perfunctory diplomatic talking points. Although concerns about discrimination, communal tensions and citizenship were acknowledged, there appeared to be limited understanding in many diplomatic discussions of the geographical and postcolonial nuances underlying the crisis.

This began to change with the outbreak of communal violence in May 2012, which dealt an early blow to Myanmar’s fragile democratisation process. The developments gradually compelled interlocutors to recognise that the country’s transition was not simply about moving away from military rule or introducing electoral reforms. It also involved confronting deeply entrenched postcolonial challenges, competing historical narratives, unresolved questions of identity and citizenship, and the complex relationship between the centre and its ethnic peripheries.

The Rohingya question could not be understood simply as another episode of communal tension between religious communities. It was deeply embedded in the history of colonial-era migration, the changing political geography of the Arakan region, competing narratives of belonging and the post-independence construction of citizenship in Myanmar. The historical relationship between the territories that now constitute Bangladesh and Myanmar, population movements during British colonial rule and the subsequent politicisation of identity were essential to understanding the dispute. The tendency to reduce the issue to a humanitarian concern or communal violence obscured these deeper historical and political dimensions.

The ICJ verdict takes me back to August 25, 2017. At the time, a colleague and I constituted a two-member Political Affairs team working on Myanmar at UN Headquarters. We were engaged in preparations relating to the UN response to the Kofi

articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Author and storyteller Vinita Zutshi revisits Kashmir’s oral traditions in a collection of 18 folktales, bringing its characters, customs and storytelling heritage to a new generation of readers

The absence of a familiar story can sometimes reveal how much of a culture has slipped out of everyday conversation. For author and storyteller Vinita Zutshi, that realisation came while she was conducting storytelling sessions in Kashmir. “Teachers spoke to me about children who could no longer speak Kashmiri. The families acknowledged that many of the stories passed down by their elders had never been recorded,” says Vinita. The discovery eventually became the starting point for a literary exercise that would take her into the world of Kashmiri folklore.

Her book, Folktales from Kashmir , brings together 18 traditional narratives that have travelled through generations, largely through oral storytelling. Published under Red Panda, the children’s literature imprint of Westland Books, it is a 178-page illustrated collection. Illustrated by Charbak Dipta, the book introduces young readers to an assortment of characters, including foolish kings, clever tricksters, ambitious old women, daring daughters, jackals and unlucky thieves. The stories combine humour, everyday situations and elements of magic, with observations on human behaviour woven into their narratives.

She subsequently began looking for people who could share these narratives. Conversations with families revealed that parents and grandparents had carried the stories in their memories, but few had thought of preserving them in the written form. One interaction with a student, who spoke about her mother collecting stories in a village near Pulwama, particularly surprised her. “She was a repository of fascinating stories. Eventually, I came across another elderly woman who shared her own collection of tales, and that is how my journey of discovering and documenting Kashmiri folktales began,” she recalls.
Author and storyteller Vinita Zutshi who revisits Kashmir’s oral traditions in a collection of 18 folktales. She will be a part of Vizag Junior Literary Festival. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

The project has a personal dimension for Vinita, who describes her engagement with Kashmiri folklore as a process of discovering her own cultural inheritance and her Kashmiri roots. “I grew up across different parts of the country, but Kashmiri was not spoken at home by my parents. English and Hindi became our languages of communication,” she says. Her interest in collecting these stories grew from an awareness that a considerable body of traditional knowledge remained undocumented.

The collection also reflects her interest in the way traditional stories engage with human nature. Vinita points out that folktales rarely depend on flawless heroes. Their characters are recognisably human, with practical concerns, ambitions, weaknesses and occasional lapses in judgement. “Not all heroes have to be strong. The characters in Kashmiri folktales are very practical and rooted in everyday realities. They have their own shortcomings, and that is what makes them interesting,” adds Vinita. Some narratives have unexpected turns, while others use humour to examine greed, vanity and the consequences of one’s choices.

For Vinita, this range of emotions is particularly relevant to contemporary childhood. “Resilience is missing in children today. Parents are often unwilling to talk about difficult emotions and tend to step in at every instance of discomfort,” she says. Stories, she feels, can gently introduce children to situations involving disappointment, uncertainty and difficult choices. Classic fairy tales such as Hansel and Gretel and Cinderella have characters and settings that may feel culturally distant to Indian children. Folktales rooted in Indian traditions, she argues, give them another cultural context through which to explore similar experiences.

An author of 22 books, Vinita is also a performance storyteller, editor, speaker and transformational parenting coach. Her storytelling performances, which she has presented to audiences in India and abroad, rely on voice, expression and characterisation rather than puppets or props. She believes that an audience should be able to see an entire story unfold through the spoken word.

Vinita will bring this approach to Visakhapatnam at the seventh edition of the Vizag Junior Literary Festival on November 21 and 22 at Hawa Mahal, Beach Road. Her storytelling sessions will offer young participants an opportunity to experience the oral tradition and engage with stories through performance.

For Vinita, the larger purpose of sharing these narratives is to keep stories in circulation. “A folktale survives when someone chooses to tell it again and when another generation finds a reason to listen,” she adds.

Vizag Junior Literary Festival will be held on November 21 and 22 at Hawa Mahal, Visakhapatnam. Vinita will be conducting open as well as registered sessions during the fest. It is on from 10am to 7pm.

articles.title: Heritage is not just Lutyens, but also books at the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library, SC tells government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Centre says it values the books as a treasure; the library has tomes dating back to 1702

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) told the Union government that culture is not confined to preserving the Lutyens neighbourhood in the national capital but extends to protecting centuries’ old books of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library that are about to lose their home.

Appearing before a Bench headed by Justice Sanjay Kumar, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati agreed with the court that the books are a “treasure that we love”. The government repeated its November 16 undertaking to the court to not shift the book from its premises in Shastri Bhawan.”
“We are more concerned about the books. Heritage is not just the Lutyens... There are books dating back to 1702,” Justice Kumar expressed the court’s concern.
Mr. Mehta assured the court that the government was conscious of the weight of cultural value and heritage the books represent.

“The government will sit with the amicus curiae, senior advocate Haripriya Padmanabhan, and resolve the issue. Meanwhile, we stand by the undertaking given to the court on November 16,” Mr. Mehta assured.

Justice Kumar said the case was taken up by his Bench on a suo motu basis. However, his Bench did not have the public interest litigation (PIL) roster. The judge said the suo motu case would now be referred to the Chief Justice of India, who would allocate it to the appropriate Bench. Justice Kumar said it may likely come back to his Bench, but urged the government to hold true to its November 16 undertaking in the meanwhile.
The suo motu case was initiated on the basis of reports that the library was asked to vacate by September 30 as part of the redevelopment project.

On November 16, the court had observed its intention to examine the government’s proposal to permanently relocate the library to the under-construction Kartavya Bhawan-4 in Central Delhi as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project.
The Centre’s affidavit in the apex court had informed the court that space had been earmarked for both the Central Secretariat Library and the Tulsi Sadan Library in the proposed Kartavya Bhawan-4.

According to the affidavit, approximately 5,583 sq. m. has been allocated for the two libraries, comprising 4,112 sq. m. on the ground floor and 1,471 sq. m. on the first floor, compared with the 5,209.58 sq. m. they currently occupy. The government said the construction contract for Kartavya Bhawan-4 had been awarded and the building was scheduled for completion by December 2028.
Until then, books from the Central Secretariat Library were proposed to be shifted temporarily to the General Pool Office Accommodation complex in Netaji Nagar.
Ms. Padmanabhan, while narrating her visit to the facility where books from the Tulsi Sadan Library were stored, described the conditions as “atrocious”.

articles.title: ‘O.M Operation Mole’: Is Mammootty’s casting in the Dhanush-starrer justified?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dhanush’s ‘O.M’ marks Mammootty’s return to Tamil cinema after seven years
( Spoiler alert: This piece contains spoilers about ‘O.M Operation Mole after its first screening)

Tamil director Rajkumar Periasamy ’s most-awaited film, O.M Operation Mole , was released to much fanfare on Friday (November 20). The film had generated considerable hype, especially for its star-studded ensemble, including Dhanush , Mammootty , Sai Pallavi , Indrans, and Naseeruddin Shah. In particular, Mammootty’s casting (marking his return to Tamil cinema after seven years) has been a major talking point.

In the film, Mammootty plays Burma Karthikeyan, a notable smuggler who mobilises red sandalwood from the forests of Andhra Pradesh. Under the scanner of Sai Pallavi’s IPS Nithya Reddy, Karthikeyan is unaware that his operations are being scrutinised and that his close confidante, Thirukumaran (Dhanush), is an undercover agent named Pazhanivel who has infiltrated his gang as part of the titular Operation Mole.

Right from the beginning, the writing elevates Karthikeyan as a major smuggling mogul with political power. Though the character gets a lion’s share of screen time and narrative purpose in O.M , the film underserves the actor. Firstly, conveniences in the writing of Karthikeyan’s equation with Thiru don’t paint the image of a seasoned smuggler who knows what is at stake. At one point, Karthikeyan becomes a mere pawn in a game he isn’t even aware of.

The emotional bond between Karthikeyan and Thiru becomes quite central to the plot and provides Mammootty with some substance to work with, but the question remains whether it was necessary to cast a star of his stature and a performer of his calibre for this role.

During a pre-release event ahead of the film, Mammootty had joked that his character in the film hardly does anything other than order his subordinates around. Now we know that he wasn’t joking; the superstar is so incapacitated in the film that watching him perform that odd kick or join Dhanush in a dance sequence feels like a relief.

Fans of Mammootty should watch out for how he emotes in two pivotal scenes at the end, one set in a courtroom and another inside a prison. That Mammootty proves to be a treat to watch despite these issues tells us that the actor in him deserves better films.

articles.title: SC asks Centre for response on bringing in law on marriages between those closely related by blood
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also noted that the court can't regulate such 'consanguineous marriages'

Saying it did not want to direct but only sensitise the Government, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) asked the Centre for its response on the "desirability" of bringing in legislation on marriages between those who are closely related by blood.

A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also noted that the court can't regulate such 'consanguineous marriages'. That falls exclusively within the domain of the legislature, the SC said.
The Counsel for the petitioner who flagged the issue said it raises inter-generational equity and people should be informed about the adverse consequences through wide publicity.

"We are issuing notice for the limited purpose of impressing upon the Union of India to consider the desirability of bringing a suitable legislation, or to ensure wide publicity through different channels, including a proper curriculum...," the Bench said.

"We can issue notice for the limited purpose of impressing upon the Union of India to consider the need for a suitable legislation. We will not direct them. We will only sensitise them," the Bench observed.
The petitioner's Counsel said certain safeguards should be provided as the practice of consanguineous marriages was increasing.

articles.title: This is not the Congress of Dec. 6: Azam Khan backs alliance, takes ‘biryani’ swipe at Owaisi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The senior SP leader hits the ground running, jabs at the Owaisi-Azad alliance, softens stance on Congress

Taking a swipe at Asaduddin Owaisi’s political ambitions in Uttar Pradesh, senior Samajwadi Party (SP) Azam Khan has stated that people in his region do not prefer “Hyderabadi biryani” and instead favour “pulao and mutton biryani”.
Following his release on interim bail, Mr. Khan returned to Rampur and outlined his political stance ahead of the assembly elections.
Addressing reporters at a press conference on Thursday (November 19, 2026) he dismissed the electoral prospects of Samajik Parviartan Morcha while striking a reconciliatory tone with the Congress.
When asked about the coalition with the Congress for the upcoming State polls, Mr. Khan expressed openness to an “honourable understanding and a respectable seat-sharing arrangement.”

Explaining his positive outlook toward the party, Mr. Khan noted that he shared good personal relations with current Congress leaders, stating, “This is not the same Congress that remained silent on December 6 (1992) during the Babri Masjid demolition, or under whose rule the Maliana and Hashimpura communal riots (in Meerut,1987) occurred. Today’s leadership is different.” Mr. Khan further said he was willing to make concessions, even “sacrificing” additional seats if necessary to secure a dignified agreement.

Expressing faith in the judiciary, he hoped he would be able to contest the polls and said the upcoming elections will be fought on public issues affecting youth, farmers, and women, rather than solely along caste and religious lines. While the SP has put forward a development programme, the BJP is only responding with hate. If you touch your television screen, you can feel the heat,” he remarked.

Reacting to Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya’s remark that interim bail does not amount to acquittal and that “criminals will not be allowed to roam freely,” Mr. Khan struck a sarcastic tone. “I am well aware of my status. I am just grateful to be alive,” he said, before reminding the BJP leader of how criminal cases against Mr. Maurya and other party leaders were withdrawn after the BJP came to power in the State.

Earlier, Mr. Khan challenged the authorities to “bring the bulldozers and raze every single building” of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. He argued that 90% of the university was built between 2004 and 2006, and challenged the Income Tax Department’s campus valuation, noting historical construction costs were significantly lower than current CPWD rates. He rhetorically stated that he was considering withdrawing his ongoing lawsuit against the Rampur Development Authority (RDA) so the world can see what happens to educational institutions built by a Muslim.

articles.title: How ports and cyclones are eating away the beaches of Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly 31% (318.96 km) of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline is eroding, with about 91.6 km falling into the ‘high erosion’ category. While the losses are concentrated in the delta districts of Kakinada, West Godavari, and Krishna, the coastal port district of Visakhapatnam is also facing the issue. Paul Nicodemus explores how decades of port development, changing wave patterns, and cyclones have contributed to the erosion of the City of Destiny’s beaches

For Professor B.S.R. Reddy, who retired from the Department of Meteorology and Oceanography at Andhra University, reaching the sea from the Beach Road in the early 1960s meant walking at least half a kilometre over high dunes—an exciting journey up one sandhill and down another. Residing at the Pithapuram Beach Hostels as a student, opposite the site where the INS Kursura Submarine Museum now stands, he recalls hearing the crashing waves from the road amidst the shouts of fellow students playing football on the sand, even though the sea itself was hidden from view. Today, he says, there are “no beaches” along stretches of that road, and the waves strike it directly.

Beyond the disappearing stretches of sand, the consequences of coastal erosion are being felt not only by those who depend on the sea for their livelihoods, but also by the State, which is steadily losing land to the encroaching sea.

For instance, earlier this month the seaward edge of the beach road near the museum had been cut away, with rubble and boulders strewn across the sand below. Near RK Beach, waves had eroded a sand bank beneath a row of coconut palms, exposing the bases of trees and cable conduits.

This loss is also documented in the Shoreline Change Atlas of Andhra Pradesh, published in February 2024 by the National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR), under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences. Using satellite imagery, the agency mapped 1,027.58 km of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline between 1990 and 2022. It found that 31 per cent (318.96 km) is eroding, 24.9 per cent is stable, and 44 per cent is gaining sand—with about 91.6 km falling in the “high erosion” category, losing more than five metres a year.

According to the atlas, the losses are concentrated in the delta districts. In Kakinada, 52.8 per cent of the coast is eroding, followed by West Godavari at 52.5 per cent, and Krishna at 43.8 per cent. It mentions that coastal port district Visakhapatnam lies somewhere in between. Of its 70.61 km of coast, 25.9 per cent is eroding, mostly at a rate of 0.5m to 3m a year; 51.3 per cent is stable and 22.8 per cent is gaining sand. The district map identifies one erosion hotspot at Pedanagamayyapalem near Bheemunipatnam.

articles.title: Rohingya in Bangladesh welcome UN court’s genocide verdict but say they want to go home to Myanmar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: “The Rohingya have their own distinct culture, their own language, their own land and everything else that defines an ethnic group,” said a Rohingya community leader

Hundreds of Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh sat in front of a big screen at their sprawling camp in Cox’s Bazar, watching the news from the Netherlands, where the U.N.'s top court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority in a brutal 2017 military operation.

For many, the historic verdict on Thursday (November 19, 2026) represented a “small victory” — offering a glimmer of hope that someday they would be able to return safely to their homes in Myanmar, across the border from Bangladesh.
It was a landmark judgement, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya — the first time the court ruled that a state committed genocide.

A Rohingya refugee gives a thumbs up while another person holds a placard following the announcement of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) verdict, in a case accusing Myanmar of committing genocide against the minority Rohingya population, at a refugee camp in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, November 19, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

The Hague-based International Court of Justice also ordered Myanmar’s military-supported government to allow the Rohingya to return home safely, pay reparations to the Rohingya Muslims and prosecute those suspected of having committed genocide.

But it remains to be seen how much of the ruling can be implemented. The court’s rulings are final and legally binding, but it has no way to enforce them beyond reporting noncompliance to the U.N. Security Council.
There was no immediate reaction to the ruling from the Myanmar delegation in The Hague or from the government in Myanmar.
At the refugee camp in Cox’s Bazar, Rohingya refugees told The Associated Press of their concerns.

Mohammad Rofik, a Rohingya community leader at the camp, said the verdict was “a victory” for them as it recognised the genocide and the sufferings of their minority in the Buddhist-majority nation, but that it was “not an end” to their ordeal.
“Justice has started,” Mr. Rofik said, adding that the Rohingya still have “a long way to go.”
For Sayed Ullah, another Rohingya community leader, the verdict was a historic recognition that the Rohingya are a distinct ethnic group.
“Myanmar denies the existence of the Rohingya, but now the (U.N.) court made it clear," he said.
