articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the expected upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.
Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22–23

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.
Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.
Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.

articles.title: U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

Migrants deported by the Trump administration to countries other than their own have endured hunger, thirst and other deprivations while being detained indefinitely in places with poor human rights records and little oversight.
For those expelled to South Sudan, and their families, the ordeal has come at an additional cost.

Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones. Instead, the guards pocketed most of the money, families said, while detainees went for days without food or clean water, and months held incommunicado.

“They used our desperate situation,” said Ngoc Phan, a U.S. citizen whose husband Tuan Phan had been detained in South Sudan for nearly a year before he was repatriated to Vietnam in June. “If that's not exploitation, I don't know what is.”
It is the inevitable outcome, she said, of a U.S. immigration policy that places deportees in the custody of countries struggling with poverty and corruption, then looks the other way.

Five deportees remain in custody in South Sudan, a country in East Africa where millions face severe hunger and poverty after years of civil conflict and devastating floods. The economy is in tatters, and government workers rarely receive wages.

In all, Ms. Ngoc Phan said she forked over roughly $4,000 intended for food, water and a cellphone. She sent several hundred dollars on multiple occasions and each time, her husband said, guards would give him a few bananas and apples, and some peanuts.

Mr. Tuan Phan, 44, said he lost 20 pounds while under confinement at a gated three-story building in Juba, the capital, and that tensions grew between detainees and guards as living conditions worsened.

One detainee who wanted a window open for fresh air was struck in the face by a guard, and another who complained about a lack of soap was locked in his room for days and only let out to eat, he said.

In addition to the Phans, The Associated Press interviewed six other people familiar with the treatment of detainees in South Sudan, including relatives and lawyers. Most spoke on condition of anonymity for fear of retaliation against the detainees.
AP also reviewed money-transfer receipts and messages between guards and four detainees' relatives.

When asked about AP' s findings, a spokesperson from South Sudan's Foreign Ministry said detainees are given adequate food, water and medical care, and are allowed regular contact with relatives and lawyers while it works to resolve their individual cases. The spokesperson said the Government pays for all the associated costs.

articles.title: Asian American women feel impact of Nvidia CEO affair scandal, 'spy' accusations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It’s a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes

The reveal earlier this month that billionaire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had extramarital affairs sent shock waves through the tech world, particularly with Asian Americans who revered him as a once-in-a-generation talent.
But what has hit hard for Asian American women is the discourse around the allegation that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman at the centre of the scandal, was possibly a spy.
Almost immediately, videos and memes reviving tired tropes fetishising Asian women hit social media.

“So few Asian women in general make it to the news for positive things. This is just going to continue to perpetuate negative stereotypes or biases for Asian women," said Misa Chien, founder of a network for Asian American women leaders called The Authentic Asian. Whether or not the allegation is true, “just the news will definitely influence people's opinions of women who have broken the ceiling or are trying to.”

Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It's a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes.
Jensen Huang has since resigned . However, the U.S. Justice Department has not found sufficient evidence that Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, was a spy.
“I don't know if that's been determined yet," President Donald Trump told reporters this week.

Among the social media posts being spread was a collage of photos showing CEOs with Asian female partners. Author May-Lee Chai, who has written about the treatment of Asian women throughout history, called it “disgusting.”
Depicting them like trophy wives "implicates these spouses like they're somehow similar to this suspected spy,” said Ms. Chai, a creative writing professor at San Francisco State University.

The speed at which people glommed onto the Asian female spy narrative was shocking to April Moh, chief marketing officer for a financial technology company and board member of Stand with Asian Americans, a legal civil rights organisation specialising in combating workplace anti-Asian discrimination. The chatter has also led to women sharing stories of uncomfortable interactions.

“I have women in technology who tell me that they get really weird looks and they get questioned about laptop security by their colleagues when they're visiting China,” Ms. Moh said. “I have another person telling me that she has been jokingly asked, 'So, are you a spy?' by people who think that's a joke now. It's not funny to her or me.”

Many clients of Stand with Asian Americans are Asian women who have proved their competence yet are still accused of being fraudulent or deceitful, said Rachel Lee, the organisation's president and general counsel.

articles.title: Pakistan Climate Minister arrives in Delhi to attend SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27; the event, which will be inaugurated by PM Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun

Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Masood Malik , arrived in Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026) for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum, officials said.
Mr. Malik is representing Pakistan at a cultural meeting of the SCO in Delhi, the Pakistan High Commission in India said.
Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27.

The SCO is represented by China, India, Russia, Iran, Pakistan, Belarus, and Central Asian countries such as Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan. Almost all the member countries of the SCO are ancient civilisations that date back to the BCE era.

The dialogue, which will be organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs, was proposed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the SCO leaders’ Summit in Tianjin last year and adopted by the SCO Council. According to the sources, the government has invited Pakistan’s Minister for National Heritage and Culture Aurungzeb Khan Khichi, for the event. Culture Ministers from the 10 member states, including China, Russia, Iran, Belarus and Central Asian states, 15 Dialogue partners and observer countries have been invited.

The event, which will be inaugurated by Mr. Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun. The fort is also the site of many excavations showcasing India’s ancient past spanning nearly 3,000 years, from the Pre-Mauryan, Mauryan, Sunga, Kushana, Gupta, Post-Gupta period to medieval-era Rajput, Sultanate and Mughal periods, officials said, explaining its importance.

articles.title: Rare ‘bridal veil’ bamboo mushroom spotted near Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A biologist stumbled upon the elusive and short-lived bamboo mushroom in Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary earlier this week.

S. Gagana, biologist and nature education officer at Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary in Srirangapatna, described the sighting amidst the woodland floor of the bird sanctuary on November 17 as a “delightful encounter.”

“With its dark cap, white stalk and delicate lace-like skirt, the mushroom looked like a tiny bridal veil amidst the forest floor. It was indeed a fortunate moment to witness this fascinating fungus in its natural habitat,” she said.
Scientifically known as Phallus indusiatus, the bamboo mushroom, popularly referred to as “veiled lady” or bamboo pith, derives its common name from its close association with bamboo thickets.

“However, it can also grow in other moist, shaded habitats rich in decaying leaves and organic matter. The net-like structure surrounding its stalk is called an indusium, which gives it the distinctive appearance of a veil,” Gagana explained.

Deputy Conservator of Forests (Mysuru Wildlife Division) Prabhu Gowda noted that the fungus grows on deadwood bamboo when moisture and temperature conditions are favourable, adding that it also emits a distinctive odour.

Interestingly, the bamboo mushroom is considered a delicacy in several Asian cuisines and is used in soups and stir-fries after proper processing. However, Gagana cautioned that wild mushrooms should never be consumed without expert identification.

C. Hemavathi, retired professor of Botany at Government First Grade College in Mysuru, confirmed the species identity, noting that while the fungus is not uncommon in wetter regions like Kodagu, its emergence in Ranganathittu’s riverine habitat is noteworthy.
“The sighting reminds us that Ranganathittu’s biodiversity extends well beyond its avian visitors, and even the forest floor holds fascinating wonders waiting to be discovered,” Ms. Gagana said.

The Smart 4 Pro sports a 13MP rear camera and a 5MP front camera.
Lava Smart 4 Pro has been priced at ₹10,999. It will be available in Neelam Blue and Konark Gold colours.

articles.title: If AI lifts productivity, will demand sustain growth?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Tugan-Baranovsky argued that machines can produce machines which can produce more machines, while Luxemburg contended that machines are not an end in themselves; only time will tell who is right

Building on our previous piece yesterday, we now look at the macroeconomic implications of rising labour productivity on the global economy. We make the global economy our canvas to avoid between-country gain/loss that AI may result in since that is not the purpose of this piece. Our basic question is what may happen to the global pie of output and jobs. When looked at globally, demand consists of consumption, investment, and government expenditure because the trade component cancels out. (Refer Infobox below)

Since government intervention is outside the sphere of “pure” market economy, we focus on consumption and investment. The question we pose in this piece is how a rise in productivity would affect this demand? By its very nature, this piece is speculative, so we present two opposite cases for the readers to mull over.

A rise in labour productivity, without a commensurate increase in real wages, means a fall in the share of wages (denominator of the last term rises but the numerator does not rise in tandem in Infobox below). The implication of this is significant for consumption growth.

Let us say the total output of 100 is divided equally between workers and capitalists and, for the sake of the argument, workers consume all their wages and capitalists consume half of it. The total consumption demand would be 75; 50 by the workers and 25 (half of 50) by the capitalists. Suppose AI is introduced in this economy which increases workers’ productivity dramatically but the wages rise by less than that, so the wage share falls to, say 30%. The consumption demand of the workers fall to 30, whereas for the capitalists it rises to 35 (half of 70), totalling to 65. Demand for consumption falls from 75 to 65, so demand worth 10 just disappears into thin air.

More than a century ago, a theoretical debate took place between Rosa Luxemburg, a German Marxist, and Mikhail Tugan-Baranovsky, a Russian economist on the issue of falling share of consumption in total demand and growth in a capitalist economy. It would be apt to revisit that debate in the context of AI and rising labour productivity.

Tugan-Baranovsky argued that even if the share of consumption falls, investment can replace the lost demand. The 10 units of consumption goods that vanished into thin air above could simply get replaced by investment demand. He went to the extreme to argue that machines can produce machines which can produce more machines even if the demand for the final consumption goods they produce shrinks over time. The case of AI, imagined as machines producing more machines, comes very close to what he had in mind.

Luxemburg argued, on the other hand, that machines are not an end in themselves. If the demand for the final consumption goods they produce is decreasing over time, there will be a surplus of such goods piling in the warehouses. The 10 units of consumption not sold will not be produced next time. And if they are not produced, then the machines which could produce them will lie idle. This would dissuade the capitalists from making more machines. Let alone machines producing more machines for the sake of it, there will be a contraction of investment in machines.

The implication of her argument is clear. Of the two sources of demand, investment is unique. It creates both the capacity to produce output (say a factory which produces motorcycles) and the demand for output (construction of the motorcycle factory gives rise to demand for goods like cement, steel etc. which goes into building the factory). Looking at the level of the economy, if the capacity to produce output expands faster than the demand for it, there will be a contraction of investment eventually.

To be sure, there are other possibilities. None of this may happen if one of the following conditions holds. One, while productivity rises in the sector affected by AI, it may give rise to demand in sectors where labour productivity is quite low. Seen at the macro level, total labour productivity, which is the average of high labour productivity in AI sectors and lower productivity in the rest of the economy, may remain the same as it was in the pre-AI age. Two, even if overall labour productivity rises, wages rise in proportion, in which case the very source of a fall in the wage share disappears. This seems unlikely under capitalism though. Three, even if the wage share falls, investment demand could replace the lost consumption demand because AI requires more intensive capital investment to cater to the final demand.

Even though it is difficult to isolate specifically which component of investment is exclusively associated with AI, there is a broad consensus in the literature that the bulk of it would show up under the category computers and peripherals. The Chart below shows that investment in AI seems to be off the charts compared to any other component of investment. For comparison with other components of investment and GDP, we have created an index which starts at 100 in 2021 for all the variables under consideration. While nominal GDP has risen 1.5 times, investment in AI has risen 3.5 times within a short span of less than two years.

AI in the chart is expenditures on “Computers and peripheral equipment”. 2026 Q3 is BEA’s advance estimate. Chart: Azad & ChowdhurySource: Authors’ calculations. U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), retrieved from FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

There are issues we have not touched upon in this piece. One, the ecological crisis that AI may lead to, in terms of electricity generation and water usage, is being considered to be devastating. Two, precisely for reasons of the ecological crisis, the global North may push the crisis to the South by setting up data centres there instead of their own countries, thereby replicating a colonial pattern of trade. Three, even though there may be a global slowdown induced by AI, some countries may gain at the expense of others. Four, this slowdown can be arrested through aggressive government expenditure, for example in the form of universal basic income or military spending, particularly in the global North (see infobox 1). Last but not least, this entire AI phenomenon may be a stock market bubble building to burst, much like the dotcom or subprime bubble in the US financial markets earlier.

articles.title: India’s health services has banned reuse of single-use medical devices. But who decides what’s safe?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Unsafe reuse can harm patients, and billing for a reused device as if it were new is indefensible. But there is a bigger question that needs answering: who decides whether a device can be safely reprocessed, and on what evidence?

I was at Asan Medical Center in Seoul, watching liver transplants at one of the best programmes in the world, just as my own transplant career was beginning. The surgeon fired an expensive surgical stapler, finished the job and threw the device away. I was astonished.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India’s health services has banned reuse of single-use medical devices. But who decides what’s safe?. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.
Ecological & Climate Balance: Aligning technological progress with biodiversity conservation, renewable energy targets, and climate adaptation commitments is essential for sustainable development.

articles.title: Health Ministry proposes to include antimicrobials in ‘New Drug’ definition, separate licence for bulk drug wholesale
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, and the Drugs Rules, 1945, would require manufacturers of antimicrobials to obtain Central Licensing Authority permission before applying for a State licence, amid concerns over antimicrobial resistance, and introduce separate forms for the wholesale sale of bulk drugs
The Union Health Ministry has proposed an amendment to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to include ‘antimicrobials’ in the definition of ‘New Drug’ under Rule 2(1)(w)(v).

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global public health concern and the proposed amendment has been initiated in view of concerns regarding the grant of manufacturing licences for antimicrobial products without adequate regulatory scrutiny, including the requirement for studies such as bioavailability and bioequivalence and stability studies.

The proposed amendment seeks to bring antimicrobials within the regulatory framework applicable to new drugs under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. Accordingly, manufacturers would be required to obtain permission from the Central Licensing Authority before applying for a manufacturing licence from the concerned State Licensing Authority. This is expected to strengthen central regulatory oversight and help ensure the quality, safety and efficacy of antimicrobial products.

Meanwhile, the Ministry has also proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to introduce a separate application form (Form 19-BC) and licence form (Form 20-BC) for the sale of bulk drugs (active or inactive bulk substances), distinct from the existing licensing provisions for formulations.

At present, a common licence covers the wholesale sale of both formulations and bulk drugs. The proposed amendment seeks to establish a dedicated licensing framework for bulk drugs, enabling more focused regulatory oversight of their wholesale sale and greater accountability in the pharmaceutical supply chain.

The proposal was agreed upon by the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC) in its 67th meeting held on November 17, 2025, and by the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) in its 93rd meeting held on February 16, 2026.

Under the proposed framework, the licence will capture the categories of bulk drugs handled by wholesalers, including drugs covered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The sale of bulk drugs will be carried out under the personal supervision of a competent person, thereby strengthening accountability in their distribution and handling.

“Upon implementation, the proposed amendment will: give better control over the sale of bulk drugs by way of wholesale, strengthen enforcement control in relation to antimicrobial resistance and the movement of NDPS drugs and require wholesalers of bulk drugs to obtain a separate license for sale.” Stakeholders and members of the public are invited to submit their objections and suggestions.

articles.title: Delhi HC to hear plea against demolition of Krishi Bhawan mosque
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice Anish Dayal observed that another petition pertaining to Masjid Krishi Bhawan will come up for hearing next week and deferred the hearing on the present petition by Mohd Yasir

The Delhi High Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) said it will hear on November 23 a petition seeking to protect an over-a-century-old mosque inside the Krishi Bhawan compound from demolition under the Central Vista redevelopment project.

Justice Anish Dayal observed that another petition pertaining to Qadeemi Masjid or Masjid Krishi Bhawan will come up for hearing next week and deferred the hearing on the present petition by Mohd Yasir.
The petitioner's counsel said the mosque is functional and faces an imminent threat of demolition.
The Central Government counsel stated that the present plea is an "effort to expand the scope of the previous petition", in which she is yet to receive instructions from the authorities.

In the other petition, the Centre had stated that the mosque in Krishi Bhawan had to be removed as establishment of a permanent religious structure within the confines of a government office complex was impermissible and incompatible with the "secular" character of government property.

Advocate M. Sufian Siddiqui, appearing for the petitioner on Friday (November 20, 2026), contended that the Central Government has no authority to demolish the 266 sq. yards mosque inside the Krishi Bhawan compound, even though it is not a protected monument.

There are legal hurdles that make demolition wholly arbitrary and impermissible, Mr. Siddiqui stated, as he relied upon a 1945 agreement between the then authorities and the predecessor of the Delhi Waqf Board on the usage of the mosque.
The court orally questioned the scope for judicial interference in the matter since the ownership was not in dispute and the government is redeveloping the entire area.

"Point is there is a property. Forget the religious character for the time being. That property is under somebody's ownership. The government seems to have a plan to reconstruct all these areas... but if ownership issue is not there and it's not protected, then how can (the court interfere)," it said.

The lawyer submitted that before taking action, the Centre must first show any "material breach" of the agreement to "re-enter" the premises and to determine the agreement, followed by filing of a suit.

The petitioner stated that there is continued statutory inaction by the Delhi Waqf Board and that "secularism" does not give the Centre any independent source of executive power to demolish religious institutions.

"The petitioner's case is disarmingly simple: before the Union removes the mosque, it must first establish its legal right to do so. It must honour the registered agreement, satisfy the conditions of re-entry, follow the lawful procedure for recovering possession and establish an independent authority for demolition. Until then, the mosque cannot be sacrificed at the altar of administrative convenience," the plea said.

articles.title: Class 8 student in Keralam suffers serious head injury as students clash; child rights panel seeks report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: What began as a minor verbal altercation between students inside the school premises escalated into a physical confrontation outside the school

The Kerala State Commission for Child Rights has sought a report from authorities following a clash between students of a school in Panoor, Kannur, in which a Class VIII student suffered serious head injuries after being hit with a stone.
The incident involved students of Classes VIII and IX of P.R. Memorial Higher Secondary School. The injured student was rushed to a private hospital in Kannur, where he underwent emergency surgery.

The clash took place near the Panoor bus stand on Thursday evening. What began as a minor verbal altercation between students inside the school premises escalated into a physical confrontation outside the school. The clash occurred along a passage between a mall near the bus stand and the bypass road.

During the confrontation, some Class VIII students reportedly moved into nearby houses. However, one student sustained a serious head injury when he was struck with a large stone while attempting to defend himself against an attack by Class IX students.

Local residents rushed to the spot after witnessing the incident and shifted the injured student to a private hospital in Panoor. As his condition was critical, he was immediately transferred to a private hospital in Kannur, where he underwent emergency surgery.
The child rights commission has sought reports from the Kannur Deputy Director of Education, the Panoor Station House Officer and the District Child Protection Officer regarding the incident.

Meanwhile, the Panoor police have launched an investigation into the incident. The police are examining CCTV footage from the area to establish the circumstances leading to the clash and identify those involved.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt. orders fencing around all abandoned quarries to prevent accidents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a communication to all district collectors, the Director of Geology and Mining said accidents involving unprotected abandoned quarries had been reported in recent times, which was a matter of grave concern

The Tamil Nadu government has ordered the erection of galvanised iron barbed wire fencing to a minimum height of 1.5 metres around all abandoned quarries on government and patta lands across the State to prevent accidental falls of people and livestock.

In a communication to all district collectors, T. Prabushankar, Director of Geology and Mining, said accidents involving unprotected abandoned quarries, some resulting in loss of life, had been reported in recent times, which was a matter of grave concern. Such quarries, particularly deep excavations that accumulate rainwater during the monsoon, pose a risk of drowning or accidental falls for locals, children, pedestrians, and grazing livestock.

The State government has ordered that durable perimeter fencing be erected around all abandoned quarries on government and patta lands. For abandoned quarries on government lands, the district collectors have been asked to utilise the Green Fund constituted under the Tamil Nadu Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1959, or any other available district funds to complete the fencing works as a priority within a period of two months.

The State government also directed District Officers of Geology and Mining to conduct a comprehensive field verification of all abandoned quarries on patta lands to ensure proper fencing has been erected by the respective ex-lessees at their own cost. In cases where ex-lessees have failed to comply, immediate notices shall be issued and stringent enforcement action shall be initiated, the communication said.

It also said prominent warning signboards in Tamil and English, clearly identifying the site as an abandoned quarry, specifying its depth and warning against trespassing, shall be displayed along the perimeter.

articles.title: 26-year-old man murdered by two persons in Pallavaram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: One person has been arrested; the police are on the lookout for the other
A 26-year-old man was allegedly murdered by two men at Pallavaram on Thursday (November 19, 2026) night.

A senior official from the Tambaram Police Commissionerate said the deceased, Akash, was a resident of Hasthinapuram near Chromepet and was working as a helper at the crematorium in Pallavaram. On Thursday, two people, Guru and Vimalraj, residents of Nagathamman Koil Street in Pallavaram, had come to the crematorium for a funeral procession.

The police said that after the funeral procession at the crematorium, Guru and Vimalraj allegedly stole Akash’s mobile phone, following which an argument broke out between them. Later, the two men waited for Akash to come out of the crematorium and allegedly killed him with a knife.

The Pallavaram police, after being alerted, sent Akash’s body to the Government Chengalpattu Hospital for a post-mortem examination. While the police have arrested Guru, a search is under way for Vimalraj.

articles.title: Agricultural workers’ body seeks lease payments, plots for assigned landowners in Amaravati
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly 1,800 acres of assigned land were taken over for the capital, mostly from Dalit and weaker sections, the union says

The Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Workers’ Union has demanded that the State government immediately pay annual lease amounts and allot residential and commercial plots to farmers who surrendered assigned lands for the construction of the capital at Amaravati.

In a statement on Friday, union State president D. Ramadevi and general secretary K. Lokanadham said nearly 1,800 acres of assigned land had been taken over in the Amaravati region for capital development. Most of the beneficiaries of these lands belonged to poor Dalit and weaker sections, they said.

The union leaders pointed out that the 2013 Land Acquisition Act provided for assigned landowners to receive the same rights and benefits as those holding patta lands, irrespective of whether the land was acquired through land pooling or compulsory acquisition. It alleged that the Central and State governments were violating the provisions of the law by denying assigned landowners their rightful entitlements.

The leaders said that when Amaravati was established in 2014, assigned landowners had also surrendered their lands along with other farmers, based on assurances that they would receive annual lease payments and residential and commercial plots on a par with owners of patta lands. However, these assurances had not been fulfilled so far, they alleged.

The landowners were facing severe livelihood difficulties as they had lost their agricultural land and had no alternative means of employment. The government had a responsibility to provide them relief at least by clearing the pending lease payments, the union leaders said.

They demanded that the government immediately release the lease amounts and allot residential and commercial plots to all eligible assigned landowners. Warning of an agitation, they said the union would be compelled to launch protests if the government failed to address their demands.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE: Odisha's coastal districts witness rough sea and strong winds as landfall begins
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours

According to the Indian Meteorological Department, “The cyclonic storm “Akvan” Moved nearly north-northeastward with a speed of 24 kmph during the past 06 hrs and weakened into a deep depression at 1130 hrs IST of 20 Nov over south coastal Odisha. The Deep depression is likely to move north-northeastward and gradually weaken into a depression in the next 6 hours and a well-marked low-pressure area in the subsequent 6 hours.

Ganjam Collector Keerthivasan on Cyclone Akvan, says, “Currently, the landfall process of the cyclone has reached its final stage, and the cyclone is also slowly losing its velocity and converting into a deep depression, which will further weaken into a depression going forward.
indian meteorological department said that Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over the west-central Bay of Bengal crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur.
Under its influence, isolated very heavy rainfall is likely over Odisha on 20th November.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan is likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, near Gopalpur, by noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Odisha Assembly Speaker Surama Padhy on Friday (November 23) adjourned the proceedings of the House till November 23 morning due to Cyclone Akvan, which made landfall near Gopalpur during the day.
The decision was taken at an all-party meeting, following which Padhy announced the adjournment.
During the meeting, it was decided that legislators should assist people to overcome the adverse impact of Cyclone Akvan, she said.
Odisha Assembly adjourned until November 23 morning due to Cyclone Akvan, with two-day recess for MLAs to assist affected constituencies.
Cyclone Akvan has begun interacting with the land along the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast, bringing heavy rainfall and disrupting transport services.

More than three lakh people have been evacuated across Odisha, while 423 rescue teams have been deployed. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has reviewed preparations under the state’s ‘Zero Casualty’ mission. Railway services have also been disrupted, with dozens of trains cancelled or rescheduled.
Landfall was forecast near the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts, with the system weakening to a well-marked low-pressure area in Odisha.

articles.title: U.K., E.U to announce youth mobility deal, as they discuss closer ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The two sides are expected to announce a scheme for 100,000 18-32 year olds to live and work across each other’s borders

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to agree new terms for Britain’s relationship with the E.U. as he meets with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels on November 20 at a Summit meeting. Mr Burnham has said in recent weeks that Brexit had caused “more harm than good”.

The two sides are expected to announce a scheme for 100,000 18-32 year olds to live and work across each other’s borders. In addition, they are working on closer ties in food and drink and linking the carbon trading schemes of the U.K. and the EU, as per reports.
“There’s the possibility of lower food prices, I can’t turn my back on that,” Mr Burnham said.
The summit is expected to announce the start of a dialogue on migration — including returns of irregular migrants to third countries.

The deal is a significant step to closer ties but is not expected to be the post-Brexit “reset” with Brussels that the Labour Party has sought . Mr Burnham, who is taking forward some of the discussions held with Brussels by his predecessor Keir Starmer, has committed to keeping to the red lines outlined in the Labour 2024 manifesto for the duration of this parliament (2029).

These red lines include not joining the bloc, nor its customs union and single market, and not allowing the “free movement” of people across UK-EU borders. However, Mr Burnham has said the U.K. would have to decide on its long-term options for its ties with the E.U. — including rejoining the E.U. The nature of the future relationship between the U.K. and E.U. is likely to be a campaign issue when Britain approaches its next general election.
“Business across the country have been clear, our current deal with the EU is not good enough,” said UK minister for EU relations, Hamish Falconer.

Mr Burnham had earlier said he would present legislation to the U.K. Parliament next week on this week’s agreements with Brussels. The U.K. will need harmonize some of its laws with the E.U.’s (i.e., follow them) to operationalize any deal on agriculture for instance.

fullParagraphs: The ruling by the ⁠International Court of Justice was the first time the court has held a ​State responsible for ‌genocide

A ruling by the United ​Nations' highest court that found Myanmar's ‌security forces conducted State-sponsored genocide against ​the country's Rohingya ⁠Muslim minority was unfair, a Government official said on Friday (November 20, 2026).
The decision was not ‌unanimous and Myanmar had been unjustly accused, said ‌Khaing Khaing Soe, a ‌Government ⁠spokesperson.

The ruling by the ⁠International Court of Justice (ICJ) was the first time the court has held a State responsible for ‌genocide. It came seven years after the case was filed by predominantly Muslim Gambia.
It was the ‌fourth time since the ​Nazi Holocaust that an international court ruled that the ⁠legal threshold to prove genocide had been met.
"Our country was unjustly ‌accused," Mr. Khaing Soe told a press conference in the capital Naypyitaw.
"I want to say that this decision is not a unanimous decision by ‌everyone, it is not fair."

Judges found ​that Myanmar's military carried out mass executions of men ⁠and boys, committed widespread rape and ⁠sexual violence against Rohingya women and burned or razed ‌hundreds of villages during so-called clearance operations.

articles.title: White House fires cybersecurity chief after widespread outages
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Sean Cairncross’ role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies

Cyber security chief Sean Cairncross was fired from his post, a source close to the White House told AFP on Thursday (November 19, 2026), following major outages and growing concerns about AI threats.
U.S. President Donald Trump fully supported the firing because Mr. Cairncross lacked proper credentials to perform the job, the source said.

His role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies, who has more appropriate credentials and has been Senate-confirmed, the source said.

In recent days and weeks, major outages in America have disrupted travel, communications and e-commerce for countless users, but also affected a top-secret internal communications network at the National Security Administration.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Davies on X, writing: “Congratulations to the new National Cyber Director Kirsten Davies — look forward to working together to strengthen America’s cybersecurity.”
Prior to serving as National Cyber Director, Mr. Cairncross filled various roles as a White House insider during Trump’s first term.
Prior to that, MR. Cairncross worked as the Republican National Committee’s Chief Operating Officer for the 2016 election cycle.

articles.title: U.S. religious freedom panel says ‘India targeting minorities in voter roll revisions’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding

India has escalated its targeting of religious minorities ‌during a voter list revision that struck off tens of millions ​of names nationwide, a U.S. panel on religious freedom said on ⁠Thursday (November 19, 2026).

“The Indian gov’t is targeting Muslim citizens by removing them from voter rolls, calling them ‘foreigners,’ and now illegally deporting them,” Asif Mahmood, the chair of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom, ‌said in a statement.
India’s voter list revision removed 130 million names, roughly the population of Mexico, in the largest deletion of voters in the ‌country’s history.

Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims , India’s largest minority, who ‌have ⁠faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime ⁠Minister Narendra Modi took power in 2014.
The Election Commission of India says it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue ​appeals.
The revision has become entangled with ‌a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner.

“The Indian government’s expulsion of its own citizens based on their Muslim faith is a shocking ‌escalation of tactics that target religious minorities,” said Gene Mills, a commissioner ​on the U.S. panel.
Mr. Mills urged the State Department to designate India as a “country of particular concern.”

USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding. Washington has not acted on its recent recommendations on India.

The Ministry of External Affairs has cast USCIRF as biased. New Delhi has repeatedly dismissed such criticism and called it interference in the country’s internal affairs. The Indian Embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment.

The voter roll revisions sparked protests in recent weeks, with opposition groups and student demonstrators saying the revisions affected those unlikely to vote for the BJP. Rights experts condemned India’s crackdown on the protests.
U.S. ‌Secretary of State Marco Rubio said last month the issue was a “domestic political matter” and ​Washington would not comment on it.

articles.title: Tiger ‘Explorer’ reaches Mylavaram forest near Vijayawada; four villages on alert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: GPS-enabled collar helps forest officials track the movement; no attacks on cattle or human habitations reported so far

The tiger ‘Explorer’, which has been roaming across the Eastern Ghats after travelling through several States, has entered the Mylavaram forest range in the Vijayawada forest division and was seen in the A. Konduru forest block on Friday (November 20, 2026), triggering a fresh alert among forest officials.

The tiger is staying in a hilly stretch with thick forest cover and dense bush growth. Forest officials are tracking its movements with the help of a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar fitted to it following its capture and subsequent release into the Papikondalu National Park earlier this year. Officials said the tiger had not entered any human habitation so far and no cattle deaths or attacks on livestock had been reported in the Mylavaram range.
The villages of A. Konduru, Cheemalapadu, Vinagadapa and Narkulapadu, located in the vicinity of the forest block, have been alerted as a precautionary measure.

Forest personnel are monitoring the animal's movements and keeping a safe distance to avoid disturbing it. Officials said its movement was being tracked continuously, though its next direction of travel could not be predicted.

The tiger was first noticed in the Nuzvidu range a couple of days ago and moved towards the Mylavaram range overnight. It has been staying in the A. Konduru forest block since the following morning. Officials said it could move back towards Nuzvidu or proceed towards other forest stretches, depending on its movement.

A five-member specialised tiger conservation team from Pune, which had assisted the Forest Department during earlier operations, is involved in monitoring the animal. The team is equipped to tranquilise and capture the tiger if the situation warrants it.
Forest Department personnel are also using GPS equipment, drones and camera traps to keep track of its movements.
The tiger, estimated to be about four to five years old, had earlier travelled through Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Telangana before entering Andhra Pradesh.
Believed to have originated in the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra , it was named ‘Explorer’ after its extensive journey across different forest landscapes.

After it strayed into human-inhabited areas in the Godavari region, the Forest Department launched an extensive operation to capture it. The ‘Explorer’ was tranquilised near Kurmapuram in Konaseema district on February 6 and subsequently released into the Papikonda National Park on February 14, after being fitted with a GPS-enabled satellite radio collar to monitor its movements.
However, the tiger continued to move across the Eastern Ghats landscape, occasionally approaching agricultural fields and human habitations, prompting renewed monitoring by forest officials.

Forest officials said the priority was to ensure the safety of people while protecting the tiger. They appealed to residents not to venture into the forest, approach the animal or attempt to photograph it at close quarters. They said the animal should not be disturbed and that any further intervention would depend on its movement and the prevailing situation.

articles.title: India’s smartphone sale plunged 22% during festive season
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales

As rising memory costs have been pushing smartphone prices to a new height, the impact of it was quite visible during the just concluded Indian festive season (October 8–November 10) which collapsed by an estimated 22% year-over-year (YoY), noted Counterpoint. The rising phone prices pushed a weaker demand as buyers held back their purchases.

“The decline was much steeper than the pre-festive forecast of 12%. Market value, however, stayed broadly flat YoY, as ASPs grew 28% YoY, largely offsetting the fall in unit sales,” the findings said.

The research firm highlighted that festive discounts narrowed to 10–25%, from 35–40% in 2025. “Even discounted entry-level models were generally priced higher than a year ago, putting upgrades out of reach for many price-sensitive buyers. Brands instead leaned on no-cost EMIs, bank offers and trade-ins, with 48% of smartphone sales being finance-led.”

During the first wave (October 8–18), volumes fell 19% YoY, with online sales falling short of the performance seen during earlier sale events. Online sales, which account for a significant share of smartphone purchases, declined as higher consumer traffic failed to translate into actual conversions.

During festive season also, Samsung had the best of lot with a 21% share, overtaking Vivo, as its sales fell 8% YoY against a 22% market decline. Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S25 drew strong demand, while Samsung delayed price hikes until after the sales and managed inventory better than rivals.
Vivo and Oppo declined 21% and 24%, respectively, holding up better in mainline retail through retailer incentives and bundled offers, but were weaker online.

Apple’s sales declined by double digits YoY despite strong feedback for the new iPhone 18 Pro series and continued consumer interest in the iPhone 17. However, refurbished iPhones saw strong demand as consumers sought more affordable options, which hurt demand for new iPhones.
Xiaomi declined sharply, though its sales picked up around Diwali, driven by the Redmi Note 15 and Note 17 series.
Google was the fastest growing brand in the ultra-premium segment (45,000+) as Google sold its highest ever pixel devices during festive season.
Brands with exposure to the sub-20,000 segment were hit hardest, declining by close to 50%.
Overall, the 2026 festive season was value-led rather than volume-led. Premium demand and financing supported market value, while entry-level buyers deferred purchases.

The research firm highlighted that festive discounts narrowed to 10–25%, from 35–40% in 2025. “Even discounted entry-level models were generally priced higher than a year ago, putting upgrades out of reach for many price-sensitive buyers. Brands instead leaned on no-cost EMIs, bank offers and trade-ins, with 48% of smartphone sales being finance-led.”

During the first wave (October 8–18), volumes fell 19% YoY, with online sales falling short of the performance seen during earlier sale events. Online sales, which account for a significant share of smartphone purchases, declined as higher consumer traffic failed to translate into actual conversions.

During festive season also, Samsung had the best of lot with a 21% share, overtaking Vivo, as its sales fell 8% YoY against a 22% market decline. Galaxy S25 Ultra and Galaxy S25 drew strong demand, while Samsung delayed price hikes until after the sales and managed inventory better than rivals.

Vivo and Oppo declined 21% and 24%, respectively, holding up better in mainline retail through retailer incentives and bundled offers, but were weaker online.

Apple’s sales declined by double digits YoY despite strong feedback for the new iPhone 18 Pro series and continued consumer interest in the iPhone 17. However, refurbished iPhones saw strong demand as consumers sought more affordable options, which hurt demand for new iPhones.

Xiaomi declined sharply, though its sales picked up around Diwali, driven by the Redmi Note 15 and Note 17 series.

Google was the fastest growing brand in the ultra-premium segment (45,000+) as Google sold its highest ever pixel devices during festive season.

Brands with exposure to the sub-20,000 segment were hit hardest, declining by close to 50%.

Overall, the 2026 festive season was value-led rather than volume-led. Premium demand and financing supported market value, while entry-level buyers deferred purchases.

articles.title: Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals

A two-and-a-half-year-old cheetah, KOMG 3, brought from Botswana, gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park on Friday (November 20, 2026), Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said.
Calling the development a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said it was a historic achievement for Project Cheetah.
In a post on X, Bhupender Yadav said KOMG 3 is the first cheetah from Botswana to give birth in India.
“This is a landmark moment for Project Cheetah and a proud milestone in India’s journey towards restoring a viable cheetah population,” he added.
This is the second recorded birth in the wild since the reintroduction programme began in 2022.
With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals.
“Every such birth strengthens our hope, deepens our commitment, and reminds us that conservation is a journey of patience, perseverance and collective effort,” Mr. Yadav said.
He also acknowledged the dedication, commitment and hard work of project managers, veterinarians, frontline forest staff and everyone working tirelessly for the success of Project Cheetah.

In a statement, CM Mohan Yadav said, “This is a matter of pride for Madhya Pradesh and the entire country. The birth of cubs in India for the first time by a female cheetah from Botswana is a historic achievement of Project Cheetah.

“This is an important and encouraging step towards restoring a viable cheetah population in India. KOMG 3, a female cheetah, gave birth to four healthy cubs in natural conditions after spending more than four months in the wild.”

He said this significant success was achieved due to the dedication, tireless hard work, and commitment of officials involved in the management of Project Cheetah, wildlife experts, veterinarians and frontline forest workers.
Madhya Pradesh is continuously achieving new milestones in the field of wildlife conservation and biodiversity promotion, he added.

articles.title: Bhavani Mandala Deeksha begins at Kanaka Durga temple in Vijayawada
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Devotees can receive the sacred mala at Indrakeeladri from November 20 to 24, the temple’s Vedic Committee says

The Bhavani Mandala Deeksha Mahotsavam-2026 commenced on a devotional note at the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam atop Indrakeeladri, the abode of Goddess Kanaka Durga, in Vijayawada on Friday (November 20, 2026), with a good number of devotees from different parts of the State taking up the spiritual vow on the first day.

The rituals began on the auspicious occasion of ‘Karthika Shuddha Ekadasi’ with the installation of the idol of Goddess Bhavani on the sixth floor of the temple’s Maha Mandapam. The processional deity was brought from the main temple in a ceremonial procession accompanied by Vedic chants and traditional music.
The deity was decorated with floral and beaded garlands and installed on a specially arranged pedestal amid traditional lamps and offerings.

Devotees carry the processional deity of Goddess Bhavani in a palanquin to the Maha Mandapam on Indrakeeladri in Vijayawada on Friday, the first day of the Bhavani Mandala Deeksha. | Photo Credit: K.V.S. Giri
Temple priests performed special rituals under the supervision of temple Sthanacharya V. Siva Prasad Sharma and chief priest Kota Prasad.

Following the rituals, Deputy Chief Priest Nagaraju Sastry initiated devotees into the ‘deeksha’ by conferring the sacred ‘mala’ . Men, women and children, many dressed in traditional crimson attire, participated in the rituals. Hundreds of devotees gathered at the hill shrine for ‘mala dharana’ and darshan. The temple premises reverberated with chants of the name of Goddess Bhavani.
The ceremonial proceedings, including the procession of priests and temple officials in front of the temple’s multi-tiered gopuram, added to the festive atmosphere at Indrakeeladri.
Devotees carry the processional deity of Goddess Bhavani in a palanquin to the Maha Mandapam on Indrakeeladri in Vijayawada on Friday. | Photo Credit: K.V.S. Giri

Devotees undertaking the Bhavani Deeksha observe prescribed austerities, including a simple vegetarian diet and traditional dress, for the duration of their vow. The observance may be undertaken for a ‘Mandala’ or ‘Ardha Mandala’ period and concludes with the prescribed deeksha-ending rituals.
According to the temple’s Vedic Committee, devotees wishing to undertake the Bhavani Mandala Deeksha can receive the sacred mala at Indrakeeladri from November 20 to 24.

Temple trust board chairman Borra Radhakrishna (Gandhi) and Executive Officer V.K. Seena Naik participated in the ceremony. Trust board member B. Dharma Rao, Deputy Chief Priest Kota Ravikumar, Assistant Executive Officers N. Ramesh Babu and K. Gangadhar, and Vedic scholars were among those present.

articles.title: NHAI’s AI tool to monitor road damage, follow-up complaints with contractors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is deploying an artificial intelligence-powered analytical tool to assess road conditions, identify damage to roads and pavements, communicate the information to contractors, follow up on the complaints and ensure that the issues are rectified.

As a part of a series of technical sessions at the 85th Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad, NHAI officials said Dashcam Analytics systems had been mounted in patrol vehicles to monitor highways for infrastructure-related issues. The system captures geotagged, high-resolution photographs of road conditions, pavements and road signage and uploads them to a dashboard. Each photograph is uniquely numbered. The system then communicates the information to the relevant contractor, who proceeds to rectify the issue. NHAI officials described it as an end-to-end “detection to rectification” system.

Key road conditions identified by the system include potholes and road rutting, which refers to the formation of depressed surfaces on the road. Other issues identified include edge dropping and uneven road shoulders, streetlights that are not working, signage, and gaps in road medians.

The IRC also deliberated on whether India could take a lead in road safety globally. Samrat Valani, vice-president of Development, Operations and Customer Experience, North America, Transurban, made a case for a clear mandate to halve road deaths by 2030, in line with the Stockholm Declaration on road safety adopted in 2020. He emphasised the need for a strong framework based on the “four Es”: education, engineering, enforcement and emergency care, along with political will and evidence that the initiatives were working.

Sharing examples of road safety interventions from across the world, he said that data show that in India, 54,000 people who were did not wear helmets lost their lives in last year. Citing the case of Vietnam, which he described as a “motorcycle country”, he said a government led awareness programme at around 100 schools had increased helmet use from 36% to 69% in one year.

“As the programme continued, they saw in the next year that the usage dropped to 50% and stabilised at around 57%. The point here is not the number of injuries, but the helmet use and the ability to count. What this gives us is that when you count, you get to know the effectiveness of the programme,” he said.

Touching upon the importance of quick incident and accident detection, leveraging technology to respond to incidents and clearing them as quickly as possible, he said that in the US, for every minute an incident remains on the roadway, the likelihood of a secondary accident increases by 2.8%.

Informing road users, creating awareness and measuring outcomes, adopting a fair approach by issuing warnings, particularly in cases of speeding, followed by firm enforcement, and using data to prevent crashes are important metrics, he said.

articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses Karnataka appeal against bike-taxis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench headed by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma said regulation was better than a blanket ban

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) dismissed an appeal by the Karnataka State government challenging a State High Court decision to allow bike-taxis as public transport, removing the brakes on taxi aggregators like Ola, Uber, and Rapido from offering two-wheeler taxi services in the State.
From August 2026: Bike taxi association seeks halt to crackdown, urges clear policy framework

A Bench headed by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma said regulation was better than a blanket ban. The judge said even the staff in his office opt to travel by bike-taxi rather than autorickshaws and cabs due to the considerable fare difference.
The judge noted that bike-taxis with GPS were safer for women, and two-wheeler taxis are already operating across 25 States.

The Karnataka government had found bike-taxis dangerous, saying they were not meant for public transport, considering the low safety standards of motorcycles and higher accident fatality rates. The State, represented by advocate Sanchit Garga, argued that the restriction on using two-wheelers as taxis was reasonable, proportionate, and in the public interest.

“The State has not imposed a blanket prohibition on the use of motorcycles for commercial purposes; rather, it has only restricted their use for carrying passengers. Motorcycle riders continue to have viable alternative avenues of livelihood, including under the Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025, which provides statutory protection and welfare measures for such workers,” Karnataka submitted.

A Division Bench of the High Court, in January 2026, set aside a Single Bench order from April last year, which stopped bike-taxi services pending the framing of a policy by the State. The Division Bench decision, challenged by the State in the apex court, had held that taxi aggregators and individual motorcycle owners possessed a “crystallised right to obtain permits for operating motorcycles as taxis under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988”.

The High Court had further held that motorcycles fell within the category of ‘transport vehicles’. It directed the State authorities to positively consider applications for carriage permits for motorcycles.

The State argued that the Division Bench’s January 2026 decision had effectively reduced the discretionary powers of the State and Regional Transport Authorities to grant or refuse permits to a “mere formality”.

“The statutory framework clearly contemplates that grant of permits is not automatic but subject to scrutiny based on considerations of public safety, suitability of the vehicle, and regulatory preparedness,” it contended.

The State had said the High Court had misconstrued statutory definitions under the 1988 Act by “equating motorcycles with motor cabs and contract carriages, despite the latter being vehicles constructed or adapted for carriage of passengers for hire or reward, which motorcycles are not”.

articles.title: Karnataka govt. to invest on Hassan airport, even as operations face uncertainty in other district airports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The demand for an airport in Hassan, about 190 km from Bengaluru, goes back more than six decades. Work has progressed at a snail’s pace, though land acquisition began as early as 1966. Work on the ground began in 2021, but has shown hardly any progress

The Karnataka Cabinet has decided to expand the Hassan airport project at a time when flight operations at other airports, including Shivamogga, face an uncertain future. An airport for Hassan has been in the pipeline for several decades.

Incidentally, Star Air, the private operator, ended its flights from Shivamogga Airport under the UDAN scheme on Friday (November 20, 2026), as the three-year subsidy period came to an end. The airline will continue to take bookings for the weekend on the Hyderabad route only, at commercial fares, without subsidy.

On Thursday, the Cabinet approved a revised cost of ₹542.96 crore for the project, up from the ₹193.65 crore sanctioned in 2021. It cleared an additional ₹349.31 crore, of which ₹122 crore is for acquiring more land and ₹227.31 crore for additional works and the facilities needed to operate the airport.

Excise Minister and Hassan in-charge Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda has held meetings to speed up land acquisition, which has held up the work. He has said he aims to start flights from Hassan within two years and to inaugurate the airport before his term ends.

The demand for an airport in Hassan, about 190 km from Bengaluru, goes back more than six decades. Work has progressed at a snail’s pace, though land acquisition began as early as 1966. Work on the ground began in 2021 but has shown hardly any progress in the last two years.

The first proposal for the airport was prepared by the Central Public Works Department in 1960. In November 1966, 31 acres 31 guntas of private land and 58 acres of government land were acquired for the project. In the second phase, another 12 acres of private land and 42 acres of government land were acquired in 1971.

The project received attention during the JD(S)-BJP coalition government headed by H.D. Kumaraswamy. Former Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda laid the foundation stone in 2007, after the government signed an agreement with Jupiter Aviation Services Pvt. Ltd. for construction on the build-own-operate-transfer (BOOT) model.

However, the work did not move forward. The project proponent had planned additional activities, including a golf course and a hotel, and refused to start work until the entire 960 acres required for the project was handed over. The agreement with the private firm was cancelled in 2018, when the JD(S) came to power again, this time with the Congress.

When B.S. Yediyurappa became Chief Minister, he announced ₹175 crore for the airport in his 2021 budget. The Karnataka State Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (KSIIDC) was the project implementing agency. The project has now been revised.

Meanwhile, KSIIDC Chairman S.G. Nanjayyanamath questioned the viability of airports in tier-II and tier-III cities such as Hassan and Raichur. Hassan is only two-and-a-half to three hours from Bengaluru by road, he noted, and asked whether people would choose to fly such a short distance. He raised similar doubts about Raichur. “I am not opposed to constructing airports in these cities. But I wish there were a discussion on the viability of investing so much money in such projects,” he said during a recent visit to Shivamogga.

articles.title: Replace Russian junk with American weapons system: U.S. lawmaker to India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Michael Baumgartner made the remarks on Capitol Hill in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington

India should replace its "legacy ineffective Russian junk” with American weapons systems and also opt for Boeing aircraft over those manufactured by European Airbus Industries, a U.S. Congressman has suggested.

Michael Baumgartner, a Republican from Washington state, made the remarks at Deepavali celebrations on Capitol Hill on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington.

The Deepavali celebrations were hosted by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Asian American Hotel Owners Association, Hindu American Foundations, Srimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur, Sikhs of America, Art of Living, Foundations of Jain Associations in North America and the U.S. Indian Community Foundation.

As a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Mr. Baumgartner said he regularly engages with diplomats from the Indian Embassy as the two countries seek to strengthen relations across economic and security issues.

“I was pleased to again express my thoughts that the more U.S. exports to India — from weapons systems to replace their legacy ineffective Russian junk to Boeing airplanes that are superior to Airbus to the world’s best lentils from the Palouse — the better it is for our two great countries,” Mr. Baumgartner said in a post on X.
Mr. Baumgartner also raised the issue of disruptions during Deepavali celebrations in his home state of Washington.

“A couple weeks back some attention-seeking racist morons disrupted a Diwali celebration in my home state of Washington. This evening, I was pleased to attend the Diwali celebration at the US Capitol,” he said.

The Deepavali celebrations were also attended by the U.S. Congresswoman-elect Pia Dandiya, Congresspersons Grace Meng, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Nick LaLota, Jonathan Jackson, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Norma Torres, Pete Sessions, Deborah Ross, Buddy Carter, Michael Guest, among others.
Scott Colom, who scripted history by becoming the first black Senator from Mississippi in 146 years, also lit the traditional lamp at the Deepavali celebrations.

articles.title: Economic losses from Indonesia fires could reach $30 billion, research shows
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Wildfires have burned through 7.1 million acres so far in 2026, according to the Nusantara Atlas deforestation monitor, an area 18 times the size of London

Wildfires that tore through Indonesian forest and peatland areas this year could cost the Southeast Asian country more than $30 billion, the co-author of a study on the subject said on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Losses of physical assets and from disrupted economic activity alone would cost an estimated 340 trillion rupiah ($18.6 billion), according to new research by the Jakarta-based Center of Economic and Law Studies (CELIOS).
That was equal to about 2.69% of Indonesia's GDP, the CELIOS report said.
It said additional health costs from acute respiratory infections caused by the wildfires on Indonesia's Borneo, Sumatra and Papua islands could be as high as 225 trillion rupiah ($12.3 billion).

articles.title: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkiye
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The announcement by Deputy PM Ahmad Zahid Hamidi comes a day after the UN's top court, in a landmark ruling, said that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority

Malaysia is seeking to resettle 10,000 Rohingya migrants in Turkiye as part of efforts to resolve a long-running refugee challenge involving foreign asylum seekers, the majority from Myanmar, a senior official said Friday (November 20, 2026).
The announcement by Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi comes a day after the UN's top court, in a landmark ruling, said that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority.

"Following my recent official working visit to the Republic of Turkiye, the Cabinet has agreed to a proposal to resettle 10,000 Rohingya refugees from Malaysia to Turkiye through a structured skills training programme," Mr. Hamidi said.

"I put forward this proposal as part of the government's efforts to address the situation of Rohingya refugees in Malaysia in a more coordinated, effective and humane manner," he said. Rohingya refugees will undergo a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme in Turkiye which would last three to six months.
The training will focus on practical skills that are in demand among employers across various industries in Turkiye, Mr. Hamidi said.
"With these skills, participants will be better equipped to secure employment and contribute to Turkiye's economy, subject to the country's rules and regulations," Mr. Hamidi said in a statement.
On Thursday (November 19, 2026), the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague, in its ruling, also ordered that refugees be given a safe passage home and awarded compensation.

Malaysia in late September repatriated about 1,500 Myanmar nationals under what authorities described as a voluntary programme, part of a scheme that rights groups warn could put migrants at risk by returning them to conflict-ridden Myanmar.
It was not immediately clear whether Rohingya refugees who would be selected for resettlement in Turkiye would also participate on a voluntary basis.
Mr. Ahmad Zahid however, said the initiative "is in line with the principles that guide the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in seeking lasting solutions for refugees".
This included resettlement in a third country, "with due regard for their safety, protection and dignity".
The Malaysian Government said in October it would seek clarification from authorities in Myanmar over reports that hundreds of migrants recently returned to the country were being held in detention.

articles.title: The hidden cost of handing smartphone to a child | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Paediatricians are witnessing an alarming trend: smartphones being increasingly used as “digital pacifiers” to appease toddlers during mealtime, soothe them when they throw a tantrum and keeping them engaged while managing household chores

As toddlers swiping through smartphone screens before holding a pencil has become a common sight, paediatricians are worried about an alarming trend: smartphones being increasingly used as “digital pacifiers” to appease toddlers during mealtime, soothe them when they throw a tantrum and keep them engaged while managing household chores. This phenomenon is no longer confined to urban households.

A study conducted by AIIMS Delhi, and published in the Indian Journal of Medical Research in April 2026, surveyed 282 children aged 2 to 4 years in rural Haryana. Its findings revealed that half of all the children surveyed exceeded the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) recommended screen time limit of an hour per day for children between 2 to 4 years. The research underlines a pervasive reliance on smartphones to keep children engaged, across all socio-economic layers.

articles.title: South Korea confirms first case of cholera in 10 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: It is the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001
South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly.

The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea.

The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with.

It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.

The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.
